numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With method='homomorphic', the homomorphic mask construction is backwards: the window for odd vs even n_fft sets the Nyquist bin incorrectly (win[stop] = 1 only when n_fft is odd), producing a ripple in the bandpass of the resulting minimum phase filter (visible in magnitude response; more easily seen with float32).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The magnitude response of the minimum phase filter should match the expected result without bandpass ripple; the Nyquist bin of the cepstral window should be 2 for odd n_fft and 1 for even n_fft (win[stop] = 1 + (n_fft % 2)).
trigger_conditions: n_fft set to an odd length such as N=963 (issue reproducer) or even lengths 963/964 used in the added test
float32 inputs make the ripple more visible

input_output_examples.input: h = Hamming-windowed ideal low-pass impulse response, N = 963, fc = 0.13655297795265942, minimum_phase(h, method="homomorphic", n_fft=N, half=False)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: min-phase response with visible ripple in the passband magnitude (no numeric values given in passages)
input_output_examples.expected_output: magnitude response matching the expected minimum phase result without bandpass ripple (no numeric values given in passages)

oracle_clues: Tests added in PR #24749: test_nyquist parametrized over N in (963, 964) and dtype in (float32, float64), using fc = 10 and xp_assert_close-style comparison
PR text says atol values were chosen empirically and may need tweaking for CI; no numeric tolerance given in passages
Existing test_hilbert uses xp_assert_close(m, k, rtol=2e-3)

category_specific_evidence: The PR body says the ripple is more easily seen with float32, and the new test parametrizes dtype over float32 and float64.

The fix replaces the homomorphic window construction: win[1:stop]=2 and the Nyquist bin win[stop] is set to 1 + (n_fft % 2), i.e. 2 for odd n_fft and 1 for even n_fft, replacing the earlier if n_fft % 2 branch.
The corrected window is built with dtype=h_temp.dtype, and the real part is taken with xp.real(h_temp) instead of h_temp.real.
The regression test test_nyquist uses N in (963, 964) with a firwin lowpass (fc=10, fs=100, hann window, scale=False) and failed before the fix, passing after it.

The issue reproducer uses N=963, fc=0.13655297795265942, a Hamming window, and minimum_phase(h, method='homomorphic', n_fft=N, half=False), comparing magnitude and unwrapped phase of the original and minimum-phase filters in the frequency domain.
reproduction_risks: The PR says the atol values were chosen empirically on the author's hardware and may need tweaking for CI, so no tolerance value is confirmed in the passages.
The issue reproducer depends on torch and matplotlib, and the PR says torch was removed from the minimal example, so the distilled test is the more reliable reproduction.
The expected numeric values demonstrating the violation are not stated in the passages; only the qualitative ripple and the window-formula change are given.
